title: April warmth relative to March gave no clear common link to leaf-to-bloom gaps in US Arnold Red honeysuckle in 1968-2008
abstract: We tested whether a warmer April relative to March was linked to a shorter interval from first leaf to first bloom in Arnold Red honeysuckle. We used 3,429 paired plant-year records from 412 US sites. We fit separate models for two observation networks and two periods, with plant and year effects and controls for mean spring and winter temperature. The four slopes ranged from -1.29 to +0.34 days per degree Celsius of April-minus-March temperature at fixed March-April mean. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. The later slopes were negative in both networks. The early western slope was positive and uncertain. Plant trends, adjacent-year differences, weather-grid checks, and a check with the same plants in both periods did not establish a common shortening pattern. Missing visit schedules, few eastern sites, changing site coverage, and coarse weather limit inference. Fixed monthly weather windows can extend past the events. These are seasonal associations, not causal effects of warming. We did not test air pollution, frost injury, wild species loss, or pollinator timing. The package includes paired records, coverage audits, monthly weather extracts, code, source hashes, and figures.

display.caption: Four separate tests of the link between April-minus-March temperature and the first-leaf to first-bloom interval. Left: 95% intervals corrected for four tests. Right: separate leaf and bloom date slopes on the same rows, with individual 95% intervals. Weather terms also include the March-April mean and prior winter mean. The four period labels show the actual first and last years; some later western years are absent.

Interval slopes under seven checks. These checks reuse the source records and are not independent replications. The same-plant check was added after the first models. Full uncertainty estimates are in estimates.csv.
